subject: Initial hosting ownership & network sanity check for ACME Health
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Health Network Team <netops@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial hosting ownership & network sanity check for ACME Health

Hi Vivek,

Per our kickoff earlier this week, the security and network teams asked for a compact checklist we can use to validate the private deployment (VPC/on-prem) before we hand over to production. We need items that their auditors can reference (network controls, egress filters, KMS integration, logging endpoints). Can you share a short preflight list and the network diagram you expect?

Also FYI: our procurement asked whether Redwood will accept our standard data processing addendum — I can loop legal later but wanted to surface now.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Cloud Ops, ACME Health
netops@acmehealth.com

--
ACME Health (phone redacted)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial hosting ownership & network sanity check for ACME Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the note and for surfacing procurement. Short answer: yes to the checklist and yes we typically accept standard DPAs with minor redlines.

Attached is a concise preflight workbook (redwood-private-preflight.xlsx) and a preliminary network diagram (network-diagram-v1.png). High-level items we want validated before activation:
- Ownership & contacts: named network owners, emergency contacts, and RBAC owners for the VPC and gateway
- IPingress/Egress: egress allowlist policy, approved destination endpoints, and port ranges for inference traffic
- KMS: KMS key IDs and whether ACME will manage keys or Redwood-managed CMK (please specify)
- Logging: syslog/ELK endpoints, retention window, and evidence of agent connectivity
- Audit: access audit plan, who will receive CloudTrail/Flow logs, and retention for compliance

Could you confirm the answers inline in the workbook? Once returned, I’ll assign Laura to do a network sanity pass and Ben to validate the runtime-enclave controls. If procurement needs standard DPA language, copy me and I’ll route to our legal.

Next steps I propose:
1) You fill the preflight workbook and return by 2026-08-25
2) Laura runs the connectivity sweep and returns a short acceptance note
3) Ben validates KMS and logging integrations and lists any blocking items

Thanks — I’ll also add a short access request form (access-req-form.pdf) that your team can sign to provision service accounts.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Health Network Team <netops@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T08:39:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial hosting ownership & network sanity check for ACME Health

Vivek — got the workbook and diagram, thanks. A few quick notes inline:
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (CMKs); will provide key IDs and rotation policy
- Egress: our security team requires destination allowlist; can you confirm the exact FQDNs and CIDR ranges Redwood needs to reach for model downloads and telemetry?
- Logging: we will accept Flow logs and forward to our Splunk cluster; retention set to 365 days

I’ll return the completed workbook by end of day 2026-08-25. Procurement asked that legal see Redwood’s standard DPA first — please send a copy and I’ll route.

Thanks — looping in netops for any CIDR specifics.

—
Priya

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial hosting ownership & network sanity check for ACME Health

Hi Priya / Vivek — looping in network and infra owners for the sanity sweep once we get the filled workbook. A few technical clarifications from our side that speed validation: 

1) Endpoints and ports we need (shortlist):
   - ingress control plane: control.redwood.ai:443 (HTTPS) for provisioning and health checks
   - model artifact fetch: artifacts.redwood.ai:443 (HTTPS) — outbound to these domains or to our S3-compatible gateways if you prefer
   - metrics/telemetry: telemetry.redwood.ai:443 (HTTPS) — allowlist by FQDN recommended
   - ephemeral worker egress: 0.0.0.0/0 allowed only for OS updates — otherwise restricted

2) KMS flow: if ACME provides CMKs, we need grant for decrypt/encrypt usage for service principal redwood-deploy@redwood.ai. If Redwood-managed: we supply key metadata and audit logs to ACME.

3) Access: please identify 2 network owners and one emergency contact in the workbook. We’ll prepare the ACLs and temporary service accounts once the access-req-form.pdf is returned signed.

Attachments: I’ve attached a small one-page checklist summary (also reflected in the workbook).

Laura Bennett
Networks & Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Quick follow-up after Laura’s notes: once we have the workbook answers, I’ll do a short KMS and logging acceptance test — that is, validate the CMK grants and a small test message to the provided syslog endpoint. If anything is blocking I’ll open a tracking ticket and include remediation steps.

Priya — I’ll also attach the DPA we usually send to customers (sent privately to procurement) — copying Marissa for legal intake.

Expect a short acceptance note from us within 48 hours of workbook receipt.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
